cues.subtitle: Alice and Hub register as entities on the Depository contract, each controlled by its own signing board.
cues.title: Two banks join the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Opening accounts in the settlement system before any bilateral business.
cues.what: Alice and Hub register as entities on the Depository contract, each controlled by its own signing board.
cues.why: This scenario shows the exit path: what a bank can do on its own when its counterparty stops cooperating.

cues.subtitle: Alice and Hub each hold 2,000,000 USDC of test balance as reserves on the Depository.
cues.title: Test balances credited on the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: Alice and Hub each hold 2,000,000 USDC of test balance as reserves on the Depository.
cues.why: Reserves are what a dispute is paid from, so an exit does not depend on the counterparty's goodwill, only on its reserve.

cues.subtitle: Alice opens a bilateral account with Hub and grants Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line.
cues.title: Account opened with a credit line
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral credit limit, set by the bank that carries the risk.
cues.what: Alice opens a bilateral account with Hub and grants Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line.
cues.why: Credit lets Hub owe Alice without posting collateral first. Alice alone sets how much unsecured exposure she accepts.

cues.subtitle: Hub pays Alice 100,000 USDC inside the account. Both sign the new state: Hub now owes Alice 100,000 USDC under her credit line, unsecured.
cues.title: Hub pays Alice 100,000 USDC
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral payment against a credit line, confirmed by both banks at once.
cues.what: Hub pays Alice 100,000 USDC inside the account. Both sign the new state: Hub now owes Alice 100,000 USDC under her credit line, unsecured.
cues.why: Every co-signed frame is evidence. Either side can take the latest one to the Depository without asking the other.

cues.subtitle: Alice decides to exit on her own, for example because Hub stopped responding. Her copy of the account freezes and a dispute based on the last state both parties signed is drafted.
cues.title: Alice freezes the account
cues.tradfiParallel: Invoking a close-out clause on the last confirmed position, without the defaulting party's cooperation.
cues.what: Alice decides to exit on her own, for example because Hub stopped responding. Her copy of the account freezes and a dispute based on the last state both parties signed is drafted.
cues.why: Exit does not need the counterparty. The last co-signed state is enough to claim what the account owes.

cues.subtitle: Alice submits the dispute to the Depository with the last co-signed state as evidence. Hub has 25 hours to answer with a newer state signed by both; the demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.title: Dispute filed: the challenge window opens
cues.tradfiParallel: Filing a claim with a set period for the other side to contest it with later evidence.
cues.what: Alice submits the dispute to the Depository with the last co-signed state as evidence. Hub has 25 hours to answer with a newer state signed by both; the demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.why: An older state loses only if the other side answers in time with a newer one, so each bank — or a watchtower — must watch the chain during the window.

cues.subtitle: Alice tries to send 5,000 USDC and Hub tries to send 7,000 USDC while the dispute is open. Both payments are rejected.
cues.title: Both sides are frozen
cues.tradfiParallel: A position under close-out is frozen; new trades cannot alter it.
cues.what: Alice tries to send 5,000 USDC and Hub tries to send 7,000 USDC while the dispute is open. Both payments are rejected.
cues.why: A disputed account accepts only on-chain events, so nobody can change the state that is being adjudicated.

cues.subtitle: Alice tries to finalize before the challenge window ends. Nothing is submitted.
cues.title: Too early to finalize
cues.tradfiParallel: A claim cannot be enforced before the contest period has run.
cues.what: Alice tries to finalize before the challenge window ends. Nothing is submitted.
cues.why: The window protects the counterparty: Hub must get its full time to present a newer state.

cues.subtitle: No newer state arrived. Alice's runtime submits the finalization on its own; the Depository will apply the last co-signed state.
cues.title: Window closes: finalization submitted
cues.tradfiParallel: The contest period lapses and the claim becomes enforceable.
cues.what: No newer state arrived. Alice's runtime submits the finalization on its own; the Depository will apply the last co-signed state.
cues.why: A deadline, not a negotiation, ends the dispute.

cues.subtitle: The Depository applied the last co-signed state: Hub's reserve fell by 100,000 USDC and Alice's rose by 100,000 USDC. Hub had enough reserve, so nothing was left as debt.
cues.title: Dispute finalized: Alice is paid from Hub's reserve
cues.tradfiParallel: The Depository applies the latest co-signed state mechanically; legal finality depends on governing law.
cues.what: The Depository applied the last co-signed state: Hub's reserve fell by 100,000 USDC and Alice's rose by 100,000 USDC. Hub had enough reserve, so nothing was left as debt.
cues.why: The outcome follows from signed evidence and a deadline, not from either bank's cooperation. Had Hub's reserve been short, the rest would have been booked on-chain as Hub's debt to Alice (Part 1 shows that case).

cues.subtitle: After finalization the account stays closed. A new 1,000 USDC payment is rejected.
cues.title: Account closed for good
cues.tradfiParallel: A terminated agreement: new transactions need a new contract.
cues.what: After finalization the account stays closed. A new 1,000 USDC payment is rejected.
cues.why: A finalized dispute cannot be reopened by accident. Further business needs a new account and new signatures.
